evidence.title: Regenerate a selected section of a floor plan
evidence.rawVisibleText:
Introducing Regenerate in Drafted.

Traditionally, changing one part of a floor plan meant spending hours redrawing or regenerating the entire plan.

Now in Drafted, you can select any room or area and regenerate only that section.

Drafted then explores a new way to design it, rethinking the room arrangement, proportions, connections, and flow while keeping the rest of your floor plan intact.
→ Living and dining areas not connecting well? Select both and regenerate.
→ Hallway and entry taking up too much space? Select the area and regenerate.
→ Primary suite and bathroom not working together? Select both and try a new layout.

Each regeneration gives you a new option in seconds, so you can keep exploring until the area matches your vision.

Try Regenerate in Drafted: https://www.drafted.ai

evidence.title: ESPR ban on destroying unsold clothes and shoes
evidence.rawVisibleText:
In 5 days, destroying unsold clothes and shoes becomes illegal in the EU.

And no, recycling doesn't get you off the hook. Under ESPR, recycling counts as destruction. So do incineration and landfill. Customer returns count as unsold stock.

From 19 July 2026, every destroyed apparel or footwear item needs a documented derogation, and donation comes first.

Already in force: large companies must publish annually what they discard, why, and where it goes. All categories, not just textiles.

Full breakdown in the carousel.

evidence.title: Drafted V2 launch
evidence.rawVisibleText:
Today, we’re releasing Drafted V2. The fastest AI model and experience for designing your home.

Before there’s a floor plan, there are usually a few things you already know:
“I want the garage near the kitchen.”
“I want the primary suite away from the other bedrooms.”
“I want a big open living space.”

But turning those ideas into an actual floor plan usually means a lot of time, money, and back-and-forth before there’s anything visual to react to.

With Drafted V2, you can:
 → Choose the rooms you want
 → Guide where key rooms should go and let our AI generate the rest
 → Select any area you don’t like and regenerate just that section
 → Watch your home update live in 3D while you design
 → Customize the exterior materials and generate renders
 → Generate a floor plan with our upgraded AI model, now 5x more accurate and 60% faster than our first model
 → Export your design as PDF, AutoCAD, IFC, or GLB


Generate it. Change it. Render it. Export it.

And for this update, we’ve made the entire product free to use, including exports.

evidence.title: Commercial DME enrollment process
evidence.rawVisibleText:
One of the biggest misconceptions we hear from new DME suppliers is that commercial enrollment should be straightforward after Medicare enrollment is complete. 

Unfortunately, that's rarely the case. 

Although Medicare is a proofpoint, commercial enrollment is an entirely different process.

Each payer has its own contracting requirements, timeline, documentation, and network strategy. While some large commercial carriers offer nationwide DME contracts, most still require state-by-state enrollment (BCBS). In addition to understanding which intermediary organizations are required for certain payers (think Optum for UnitedHealthCare), this creates a hurdle for DME suppliers looking to serve a nationwide patient base.

After speaking with DME suppliers across the country, we've noticed the same themes come up again and again:
• How long should enrollment actually take?
• Why does BCBS require separate contracts by state?
• What are organizations like CareCentrix and Optum, and when do they matter?
• Should I continue billing out-of-network while I wait?

We put together a practical guide that answers these questions and walks through the commercial enrollment process step by step. 

If you're a DME supplier expanding beyond Medicare, we hope it's helpful.

https://lnkd.in/eBbP_Mjj
